=== HANDOFF #6 — epic e369 (Jira Server/Data Center). READ THIS AND #5. ===

WORKTREE /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-jira-family, branch jira-family-seam @ 13ddc3bed, clean.
ALWAYS: export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"

*** THE BIG RESULT: THE INBOUND HALF OF THE HEADLINE AC IS PROVEN. THE OUTBOUND HALF IS NOT. ***

Run 30662366152 (job "jira DC harness smoke", main @ ed9d5e28d): collected=17 executed=17 skipped=0,
**17 passed** — the first FULLY GREEN DC harness run in this epic.
`test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` passes: an issue created in DC appears
in the local store with id == `_jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key)` AND the binding store mapping that
id to the DC key.

THE OUTBOUND HALF REMAINS UNPROVEN, and I checked rather than assumed:
`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py` has exactly three live tests and NONE mutates a
local ticket then asserts the change surfaces on the DC issue. [rebar:5200] (J11) must supply it.
**DO NOT CLOSE THE EPIC UNTIL IT DOES.**

WHY THIS TOOK SO LONG TO SEE — three defects masked it in sequence, each hiding the next:
  1. an EMPTY store made the pass report scanned=0 and "converged" — indistinguishable from working;
  2. the PAT-cap bug killed the suite at SETUP before the test ran;
  3. the ORACLE ITSELF COULD NOT PASS — it grepped the raw key `RBJ...-1` against a payload whose id
     is lowercased `jira-rbj...-1` and which carries no raw key at all.
Only with all three fixed does that test's verdict carry information. Its earlier RED was not evidence
of breakage, and a green before the fix would not have been evidence of function.

BOARD
  CLOSED this session: f391-806b-938f-45d8, bda8-370d-23ad-4e36 (J9), a357, 23ed-de0a-765b-49aa,
    deac-4f5a-856a-49bd, 0059-c7f0-cce1-4077 (duplicate), 2bc7-d77b-641c-42aa (preexisting).
  MERGED to main: bda8(1113) f391(1114) 8c35(1115) deac(1118) 23ed(1124) cd78(1127).
  IN REVIEW, all three LLM-Review +1 awaiting Verified: 1129 (9263 shared pager), 1130 (21fc duplicate
    -issue fix), 1131 (387d retain-on-identity-write-failure). NOTE 9263/21fc/387d are in_progress and
    are NOT children of e369 (parent=None) — they still gate "ship defect free".
  READY TO CLOSE NOW (evidence already recorded on both): 8c35-1a5e-927b-4644 and
    cd78-d877-3d25-4ec3 — the green run above satisfies their last criteria.
  STILL OPEN under e369: 5200 (J11), 5f48, 7c26 (plan CERTIFIED, ready to claim), b586 (plan written,
    not reviewed), cc77, fe15.

REPARENTED BUGS — DISPOSITION (operator asked me to wire these in)
  * 0059 "DC inbound filing is a no-op" — CLOSED as duplicate of 23ed. The observation was real; the
    candidate cause was wrong. Inbound filing works. Also corrected for the record: `filed=0` counts
    INVARIANT-VIOLATION tickets (run_differs.py:282), not tickets filed from DC issues, so it never
    said anything about inbound.
  * 2bc7 "unregistered copy of mutation.py" — CLOSED as preexisting. WE OWNED IT on file overlap: all
    three of its declared files were last modified by 199b637b5 ("0a94: pin a UserIdentityModel
    contract") = our J4. Already fixed by that commit; verified by the helper being cache-first and by
    the ticket's own reversed-collection-order reproduction passing 29/29. Needed --force-close because
    no commit names 2bc7 (the repair rode J4's commit); the reason is recorded on the ticket.
  * 5f48 "DC inbound identity mint fails silently ('jira-datacenter' is not a valid creation_channel)"
    — IN SCOPE, PROVEN by measurement, and I added **5200 depends_on 5f48**. RATIONALE: J11 exists to
    prove data moves; a SILENTLY SWALLOWED inbound identity failure is exactly the class of defect that
    would let J11 report success over broken behaviour. Fix 5f48 before trusting J11's evidence.
  * cc77 "transport params untyped" — IN SCOPE; added cc77 relates_to bda8. It is the STATIC (mypy)
    complement to the RUNTIME conformance guard bda8 added. Was on the old "outside this epic" list;
    the reparent is well-founded since it is a357's stated enabling condition.
  * fe15 "duplicated local->Jira value maps, already drifted" — in scope (Jira adapter work), no extra
    edge needed.

RECOMMENDED ORDER FROM HERE
  1. Close 8c35 and cd78 (evidence recorded; one LLM gate at a time).
  2. Land 1129/1130/1131 as their Verified votes arrive; then close 9263, 21fc, 387d.
     BEFORE closing 21fc: its plan says the create gate lives in outbound_differ. It does NOT — the
     module-size cap forced it into dispatch_one.create_one (a better site: guards the WRITE and
     reuses deferred_creates). Update the plan's Approach + that AC and record why, or the close fails
     on a stale plan.
  3. Fix 5f48 (it gates J11's credibility), then 7c26 (plan certified), then b586 (needs review).
  4. J11 (5200) LAST — it is the outbound proof and the epic's closing condition.
  5. cc77 and fe15 can land any time; neither blocks the headline.

HARD-WON LESSONS FROM THIS SESSION (all cost real time)
 1. `rebar comment` is POSITIONAL: `rebar comment <id> <body>`. There is NO --body flag — passing one
    records the literal string "--body" AND EXITS 0. SIX evidence comments were silently lost this way,
    and I only noticed because a close gate correctly said the attestation was missing. VERIFY every
    comment landed (`rebar show <id>`, check byte length). Do not trust the exit code or your own echo.
 2. A CLOSE FAILS IF THE EVIDENCE IS NOT ON THE TICKET, even when the CI run exists. Record run id +
    job name + the specific test verdicts BEFORE attempting a close.
 3. LOCAL PYTEST IS NOT A FAITHFUL CI ORACLE HERE. CI runs py3.11; this host has only 3.13/3.14.
    Python 3.12 changed runtime-checkable Protocol isinstance from `hasattr` to
    `inspect.getattr_static`, so a PROPERTY THAT RAISES breaks isinstance on 3.11 while passing
    locally. That earned a Verified -1 on cd78 and is why its guard lives in
    build_client_from_settings, not in settings resolution. When touching anything a property calls,
    assert via `hasattr` directly so the test is interpreter-independent.
 4. PRE-PUSH GATES, all of which bit: (a) module size — cap 800, LOCKED, no allowlist, and
    outbound_differ.py sits at EXACTLY 800 on main so NOTHING may be added to it; check EACH COMMIT
    independently. (b) env-var registry — docs/env-vars.md is GENERATED and records LINE NUMBERS, so
    any insertion above an env read drifts it: run `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py`. (c) commit
    subject <= 50 chars (a 52-char subject was rejected), body wrapped at 72.
 5. DIAGNOSE CI VIA THE FAILING STEP, not log greps: `gh run view <id> --repo navapbc/rebar --json
    jobs`. Log text echoes the workflow SCRIPT (including its `::error::` lines) and will send you
    after the wrong cause — it did exactly that to me on 21fc's second failure.
 6. FOUR EXISTING TESTS ENCODED DEFECTS this session (the `_envelope()` writing-mode oracle, the
    unbind-after-one-miss assertion, and three delete_issue-was-called rollback assertions). When an
    existing test blocks a fix, CHECK WHETHER IT PINS THE BUG; if so invert it preserving its INTENT
    and record why in the docstring. That is not oracle-fitting — leaving it would be.
 7. VERIFY AN ORACLE CAN PASS before trusting its RED or its GREEN — including your own new
    assertions. I nearly shipped a fourth unpassable oracle; `list_tickets` returns `ticket_id`, not
    `id`, and I checked before relying on it.
 8. `git commit --amend -F -` REGENERATES the Change-Id (forking a duplicate Gerrit change) and can
    sweep other staged files into the wrong commit. Use `--amend --no-edit` and verify the Change-Id.
 9. Bare 4-hex prefixes are often AMBIGUOUS (f391, b586, 23ed, 2bc7 all match two tickets). Use FULL
    ids. The "Error: Ambiguous prefix ..." lines in close output are harmless stderr noise from a
    merged commit's subject — read PAST them for the real result.
 10. ANOTHER AGENT SESSION runs concurrently in /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-wt-provider-seam. It competes
    for CPU and LLM gates and pushes to main. A full local tests/unit/rebar_reconciler run TIMED OUT at
    25 minutes under that contention — run targeted modules and let Gerrit's Verified gate be the
    authoritative suite signal.
